meta.name: CGM lab — GlucoSense CGM-3000 (worked example)
meta.system: Continuous glucose monitoring appliance: a wearable BLE sensor, an MQTT telemetry backbone, an HL7 clinical interface, and a web + bedside-kiosk console, all on one Raspberry Pi.
meta.author: SecureMED teaching example (CGM-LAB-INT)
meta.intendedUse: A continuous glucose monitor tracks a patient's interstitial glucose every few minutes and streams it to a display and to the clinical record. Patients and clinicians rely on it for two things: hypo/hyper ALARMS that warn of a dangerous low or high, and the glucose trend used to decide insulin dosing (including automated-delivery loops). A missed low-glucose alarm or a falsely reassuring reading can lead to severe, un-treated hypoglycaemia — seizure, coma or death. This lab is a deliberately vulnerable simulation (GlucoSense CGM-3000) that teaches students to find and fix the flaws that would let an attacker read, forge or suppress that safety-critical data.
meta.scope: In scope: the appliance's web/kiosk console, HL7 listener, MQTT broker and telemetry, BLE advertiser, on-device config and user store, and the host privilege model. Out of scope: the physical sensor hardware and adhesive, the upstream hospital EHR/LIS itself, the lab network fabric, and any real patient.

nodes.title: Untrusted lab network + BLE RF
nodes.description: Any peer on the isolated lab LAN, and the radio space around the appliance. No control is applied here.

nodes.title: GlucoSense CGM-3000 appliance (Raspberry Pi 5)
nodes.description: The device under test. All lab services bind 0.0.0.0 with no host firewall.

nodes.title: Host OS / root (SSH)
nodes.description: The Linux host the services run on. Root is the crown jewel (SEC-HAZ-009).

nodes.title: Unauthenticated network client
nodes.description: Any device on the lab LAN, and the student's Kali box. Anonymous until it defeats a control.

nodes.title: Clinician / caregiver
nodes.description: Reads glucose and hypo/hyper alarms on the console and bedside kiosk, and acts on them.

props.safetyNotes: The clinician doses insulin and responds to lows based on what the console/kiosk shows. Wrong or missing readings and suppressed alarms lead to a wrong or withheld clinical decision.

nodes.title: Hospital LIS / EHR interface
nodes.description: Upstream clinical system that queries the CGM over HL7 v2 (MLLP) for glucose results.

nodes.title: Web admin console (Flask)
nodes.description: Login, /admin maintenance token, /admin/export diagnostic download, and /kiosk/unlock. TCP 8080. Surfaces 1-4 and 8.
nodes.existingControls: SQLite-backed login with a STRONG admin password, a server-side kiosk PIN, and a 5-failure/5-min login lockout. But: the SQL is string-built (SQLi auth bypass), /admin/export joins the path with no containment (traversal leaks cgm.conf), the lockout is keyed on the spoofable X-Forwarded-For header, and app.secret_key is a rockyou word (forgeable session -> IDOR on /patient/1001-1005).

props.safetyNotes: The console is where a clinician reads glucose trends and acknowledges alarms; a compromise that alters what it shows biases a dosing decision.

nodes.title: HL7 MLLP listener
nodes.description: Answers a well-formed QRY^Q01 for a known MRN with an ORU^R01 (PHI). Serial in MSH-3; flag in NTE. TCP 2575. Surface 5.
nodes.existingControls: Requires a properly MLLP-framed QRY^Q01 naming a valid MRN and NAKs the rest. But input SHAPE is not access control: no authentication, no TLS, no peer allow-list -> any HL7 speaker gets PHI, and MSH-3 leaks the BLE XOR key.

props.harmSeverity: Minor — temporary injury, no professional intervention
props.safetyNotes: Discloses per-patient glucose results and the device serial to any HL7 speaker; wrong or leaked results can misinform a downstream clinical decision.

nodes.title: MQTT broker (mosquitto)
nodes.description: Telemetry backbone. glucose/# carries readings + alarm state; cgm/service/# holds a retained capture flag. TCP 1883. Surface 6.
nodes.existingControls: allow_anonymous false + a password + a per-topic ACL (least privilege attempted). But the password (glucose123) leaks via the config traversal and is weak; the ACL grants cgmpub WRITE on glucose/# with no READ -> eavesdrop denied but forged-reading INJECTION allowed; and cgm/service/# is readable, exposing a retained flag.

props.harmSeverity: Critical — permanent impairment or life-threatening injury
props.softwareSafetyClass: Class C — death or serious injury possible
props.safetyNotes: A recovered credential can WRITE glucose/# even though it cannot READ it: a forged 'IN_RANGE' reading masks a true hypoglycaemia, suppresses its alarm, and drives an automated-delivery / dosing decision toward under-treatment.

nodes.title: BLE advertiser (runs as root)
nodes.description: Non-connectable LE broadcast, company id 0xFFFF, carrying XOR-obfuscated manufacturer data. Surface 7.
nodes.existingControls: Payload is XOR'd rather than sent in the clear. But the key IS the device serial (low-entropy, static) which leaks from HL7 MSH-3 and cgm.conf -> trivially reversible. Obfuscation, not encryption. Service unit runs as root.

props.harmSeverity: Minor — temporary injury, no professional intervention
props.safetyNotes: Broadcasts patient-linked data over the air. Confidentiality only here, but the process runs as root, so its compromise is a host compromise (CWE-250).

nodes.title: Bedside kiosk (Chromium / matchbox on DSI panel)
nodes.description: Full-screen bedside display of glucose + alarms; unlock via POST /kiosk/unlock. Owns tty1. Surface 8.
nodes.existingControls: PIN check is server-side now (not in the page source). But /kiosk/unlock has no rate limit, lockout or delay -> all 10,000 four-digit PINs in seconds, and it returns the flag with no session.

props.safetyNotes: The bedside display is a clinician's at-a-glance view of glucose and alarms; if it is unlocked, frozen or shows the wrong patient, a low can be missed at the bedside.

nodes.title: Host shell (biomed via SSH)
nodes.description: SSH foothold + local privilege escalation to root. Surface 9.
nodes.existingControls: biomed was removed from the sudo group. But its password is a rockyou word (sunshine, dictionary-crackable over password-auth SSH) and there is a NOPASSWD sudo rule on /usr/bin/awk (GTFOBins) -> instant root.

nodes.title: User store (cgm.db, SQLite)
nodes.description: Seeded username/role/password rows queried by the login. Surface 1.

nodes.title: Device config (cgm.conf)
nodes.description: Holds the MQTT credentials, the device serial (BLE key) and a maintenance token. World-readable, one dir above the report root. Surface 3.

nodes.title: Glucose telemetry (MQTT glucose/#, retained)
nodes.description: Per-patient readings and alarm state. A forged retained message persists to later subscribers.

props.harmSeverity: Critical — permanent impairment or life-threatening injury
props.softwareSafetyClass: Class C — death or serious injury possible
props.safetyNotes: The reading and alarm state a clinician or automated-delivery loop consumes. If it can be written with no integrity control, a fabricated 'in range' value hides a real low.

nodes.title: Root filesystem / sudoers (/etc/sudoers.d, /root)
nodes.description: The NOPASSWD sudoers drop-in and /root/flag.txt (mode 600). Surface 9.

nodes.title: CGM sensor + BLE gateway
nodes.description: The wearable sensor front end that publishes legitimate glucose readings and alarm state onto glucose/#.

props.harmSeverity: Critical — permanent impairment or life-threatening injury
props.safetyNotes: Source of truth for glucose and alarms; the value a forged reading has to be told apart from.

nodes.title: Patient glucose data / PHI
nodes.description: Per-patient readings, MRNs and demographics across HL7, MQTT and BLE.

nodes.title: Hypo / hyper alarm path
nodes.description: The end-to-end path that turns a real low or high into an alarm the clinician sees and acts on.

props.harmSeverity: Critical — permanent impairment or life-threatening injury
props.safetyNotes: If a real hypoglycaemia alarm is suppressed (by a forged reading or a frozen display), the last warning before harm is gone.

nodes.title: Device & broker credentials
nodes.description: MQTT creds, Flask session secret, device serial, biomed SSH password.

flows.title: HTTP attack surface
flows.description: SQLi login, cookie forgery + IDOR, path traversal, rate-limit bypass, kiosk unlock.

flows.title: Console session
flows.description: Clinician reviews glucose/alarms and administers the device.

flows.title: Bedside interaction
flows.description: Clinician glances at the kiosk and unlocks it at the bedside.

flows.title: HL7 v2 query / result (MLLP)
flows.description: QRY^Q01 in, ORU^R01 with PHI out. Cleartext, unauthenticated.

props.harmSeverity: Minor — temporary injury, no professional intervention

flows.title: Login query
flows.description: String-built SELECT against the user table (SQLi).

flows.title: Diagnostic export / config read
flows.description: /admin/export joins the filename with no containment -> traversal.

flows.title: Console telemetry
flows.description: Console reads current glucose/alarm state to display.

flows.title: Legitimate glucose publish
flows.description: Real readings + alarm state onto glucose/<patient>.

props.harmSeverity: Critical — permanent impairment or life-threatening injury

flows.title: Retained telemetry
flows.description: Broker persists the latest retained reading/alarm per topic.

flows.title: Forged-reading injection
flows.description: With the leaked cred: WRITE glucose/# (forge 'IN_RANGE') and READ cgm/service/# (flag). READ glucose/# denied.

props.harmSeverity: Critical — permanent impairment or life-threatening injury

flows.title: Bedside display feed
flows.description: Glucose + alarm state pushed to the kiosk.

flows.title: BLE advertisement (RF)
flows.description: Non-connectable broadcast of XOR-obfuscated manufacturer data (company id 0xFFFF).

props.harmSeverity: Minor — temporary injury, no professional intervention

flows.title: Rogue HL7 query
flows.description: Any HL7 speaker crafts a valid QRY^Q01 and receives PHI + serial.

flows.title: SSH foothold
flows.description: Password-auth SSH; biomed's password is dictionary-crackable.

flows.title: Privilege escalation
flows.description: NOPASSWD sudo on /usr/bin/awk (GTFOBins) spawns a root shell.

process-web::proc-t-input.rationale: SQL injection in the login gives an unauthenticated admin session and, via the export traversal, read of on-device secrets. Network, no auth, no interaction. Scored in the CVSS v4.0 calculator as a teaching illustration.

process-mqtt::safe-alarm-t.rationale: With a leaked broker credential, forging a retained 'in range' reading on glucose/# suppresses a genuine hypoglycaemia alarm (integrity + safety impact). Adjacent network, low privilege. Illustrative CVSS v4.0 score.
